Trustee Eric Ungaro said at the meeting that the trustees had approved several projects and purchases earlier in the year despite warnings from Fiscal Officer Paul Canter, who said they may come close to their yearly budget. “We knew we were going to be running tight, cause in Poland Township, we don’t carry over $5 million like the state; I mean, they’re in the billions, we just run our budget late, and we do what we have to do,” he said. The township is projected to overspend by $1,678 at the end of the year according to their 2027 tax budget. Ungaro says the first thing trustees did upon learning of a deficit was to discontinue projects that had not yet begun. One of the purchases was a new police cruiser that trustee Edward Kempers suggested they return. The trustees also dismissed seasonal workers for the time being. “We have to do something, I don’t know if it’s personnel… I’m guessing from this point forward, we’re buying nothing that is not essential for the safety of our community,” Kempers said. The idea of a police levy arose during discussions, though one has not passed in the Township for 30 years. Canter tells 21 News that one of the biggest reasons for the deficit is the way the police department is funded. Currently, the Poland Township Police Department is partially funded by the Township’s general fund, while the other portion comes directly from local property tax revenue. The trustees do not plan to fill any vacant positions in the police department, and part-time workers are expected to reduce hours. Trustee Frank DeMain, who attended the meeting virtually, says that there is no guarantee that a levy would pass. “If we put a levy on and they vote it down, in my opinion, the residents are saying ‘Hey, we want you to do less with less or as much as you can with less’,” he said. Canter says that the township has yet to receive real estate tax revenue from the county due to changes to property tax laws that have delayed advanced collections. He adds that the township was required to fill out a tax budget for the first time in 20 years due to new state laws. Previously, the county had waived the requirement for townships to fill out tax budgets in the middle of the year. The Poland Township Trustees did not take any action at Tuesday’s meeting after Trustee Frank DeMain was unable to attend in person. Ungaro tells 21 News the trustees plan to hold another special meeting next week to discuss the financial situation and possibly make cuts. ​ Download the WFMJ app for your Apple or Android smartphone or tablet to get our push alerts as news happens. https://telex.hu/belfold/2026/08/16/leng.text: Menü Kereső Saját magát, húgát és egy férfit is kihúzott a felborult busz roncsai alól egy lengyel nő Belföld Nagy Nikoletta Állítsd be a Telexet megbízható forrásnak! Beállítom Egy borda- és gerincsérülésekkel kórházban fekvő nő kimászott a roncsok alól, majd saját maga húzta ki a húgát a balesetet szenvedett lengyel busz alól, egy férfit is kiszabadított, és összeesett – erről számolt be a túlélő az RTL-nek . A nő éppen telefonált, amikor a busz felborult, beütötte a fejét, de nem veszítette el az eszméletét. Látta, ahogy az ülések kiszakadtak a helyükről, az emberek beszorultak a roncsok közé, sikítoztak és segítségért kiabáltak, mondta. Korábban a Polsat News elérte Wojciech Tatarát, Siedliska falu elöljáróját , aki szintén beszélt egy túlélővel, ő azt mondta: másodpercek alatt történt az egész baleset. „Most kórházban van, nagyon jó ellátást kapnak, a szolgálatok gondoskodnak róluk” – mondta Tatara. A Radio ZET egy olyan férfit is elért, aki az utolsó pillanatban mondta le a medjugorjei zarándokutat, így végül nem szállt fel arra a buszra, ami balesetet szenvedett. Wiesław családi okok miatt nem indult el, de több ismerőse ott volt a buszon. Egy zarándoklat résztvevői utaztak hazafelé azon a lengyel turistabuszon, ami egyelőre tisztázatlan okból letért az útról és árokba borult az M3-as autópályán vasárnap éjjel 1 órakor, a rendőrség hivatalos tájékoztatása szerint a balesetben tizenketten meghaltak . A busz utasai lengyel állampolgárok voltak. Maciej Wewiór külügyi szóvivő azt mondta, hét sérült állapota „nagyon súlyos”, további mintegy 40 személy könnyebb sérüléseket szenvedett. A Vajdaságból indult zarándoklat résztvevői hazafelé tartottak Bosznia-Hercegovinából. A buszon 57 utas és a két sofőr utazott. Az Országos Mentőszolgálat korábban a Telexnek azt az információt adta, hogy egy embert életveszélyes, kilencet súlyos, további 37 embert pedig könnyebb sérülésekkel láttak el. A sérülteket helyszíni ellátás után a miskolci, debreceni, nyíregyházi és egri kórházakba szállítottak. Az RTL szerint az egri kórházba 6 súlyos sérültet vittek, de nincsenek életveszélyben. Debrecenben 5-en vannak, egyiküket megoperálták, a nyíregyházi kórházba pedig 20 embert szállítottak, köztük 2 gyereket, 2 embert tartottak benn koponya- és gerincsérülések miatt. Ide nem érkezett súlyos sérült, 18-an haza is mehettek a nap folyamán. Miskolcon két ember életéért még mindig küzdenek. Boncsér Sándor igazságügyi gépjármű műszaki szakértő a Telexnek azt mondta: a legutóbbi ilyen kaliberű buszbaleset Magyarországon 2003-ban történt, ekkor május 8-án Siófokon egy a Déli pályaudvarról Nagykanizsa felé tartó gyorsvonat belerohant egy német turistákat szállító autóbuszba, ami a tilos jelzés ellenére hajtott a sínekre. A balesetben 33 fő meghalt, 6-an súlyos sérüléseket szenvedtek. A buszon utazó egyetlen magyar állampolgár, az idegenvezető súlyos sérüléseket szenvedett, de túlélte a balesetet. 2002-ben is volt súlyos buszbaleset Magyarországon, ekkor júliusban egy szintén lengyel zarándokokat szállító busz Balatonszentgyörgynél 70-nel egy körforgalomba rohant. A buszvezető elaludt, a jármű felborult, 20 ember, köztük a sofőr meghalt. A járművön 52 lengyel állampolgárságú turista utazott, akik Boszniába tartottak. A Polskie Radio Rzeszów szerint a Krosnói Kerületi Ügyészség nyomozást indított a mostani buszbaleset ügyében. Az ügyészség szóvivője, Marta Kolendowska-Matejczuk a rádiónak azt mondta, hogy a lengyel igazságszolgáltatás együttműködik a magyar hatóságokkal. https://www.dw.com/en/inside-the-sea-cuc.text: Skip to content Skip to main menu Skip to more DW sites https://p.dw.com/p/5HIpq Sea cucumbers are neither cucumbers nor fish, but invertebrate marine animals with a skin or hard covering Image: oceansasia.org Advertisement When it comes to smuggling, squishy sea blobs that spend their lives eating and pooping are probably not what comes to mind. But a group of lumpen creatures known as sea cucumbers are at the center of a $200 million (€175 million) black market trade. Known alternately and misleadingly as sea cucumbers or sand fish, they are actually neither cucumbers nor fish, but echinoderms. In other words, invertebrate marine animals with a skin or a hard covering. Found in abundance around the Andaman Islands — the easternmost landmass of the Indian territory — local biologist Sangamesh Uday said they are so ecologically important that without them the intertidal zone "wouldn't be an ecosystem, it would just be broken rocks." Sea cucumbers are crucial for the local ecosystem, says local biologist Uday Image: Parinmnpa/Dreamstime/IMAGO The 1,500 or so species of sea cucumber around the world are great marine recyclers. They eat organic material including bacteria and microalgae, break it down and excrete clean oxygenated sand. This keeps vital nutrients like nitrogen and phosphorous in circulation and suppresses coral diseases. It also boosts ocean alkalinity levels which helps to slow down acidification, which is becoming a huge issue as rising levels of greenhouse gases in the atmosphere cause oceans to warm. In short, it's hard to overstate the environmental importance of these innocuous looking lumps. Why are they being smuggled? To their detriment, sea cucumbers are also considered a delicacy, especially in China and Southeast Asia. Historical records show they were traded between Indonesian fishers and Chinese merchants even 800 years ago. They are used in soups, served as pickled sides or turned into traditional medicine. And though there is some scientific evidence that the omega-3 they contain is a useful antioxidant and anti-inflammatory, they're mostly popular because they're quite phallic — and therefore considered an aphrodisiac. Sea cucumbers are considered a delicacy, used in soups or used as traditional medicine Image: oceansasia.org Since the 1980s, commercial sea cucumber harvesting has expanded globally, with better access as well as higher incomes and demand in East Asia acting as the main drivers. Though many countries have outlawed the practice, some like Sri Lanka and Madagascar do allow fishing and aquaculture. Of the existing sea cucumber fisheries, 70% have become overexploited globally. The combination of the increasing demand and legal complexities has drawn the attention of minor and major mafias. Some of the largest Mexican cartels and even the Japanese Yakuza have been reported as diversifying their portfolios by using sea cucumbers and other sea creatures to keep the money flowing. These illicit groups enter every aspect of the supply chain — from extorting fishermen to the final smuggling of illegally-caught cucumbers across borders. They exploit weak environmental regulations and a lack of official knowledge around rules and species. Sea cucumbers are sometimes marked as legal fish consignments or smuggled into countries that do allow trade in the species. Teale Phelps Bondaroff, a leading expert on sea cucumber crime, said awareness is critical in dealing with the issue. "While many law enforcement officers may be on the lookout for drugs, weapons or well-known wildlife contraband like ivory, rhino horns or shark fins, sea cucumbers may slip past," he told DW. Poachers from overseas drawn to Andaman Islands The Indian government began regulating sea cucumbers in the 1980s and introduced a blanket ban on fishing them in 2001, when it saw the impact of the illicit trade on local populations. Since then, India has become the country with the strongest protections for the species. Anyone who catches one faces a seven-year jail term — the same sentence handed down for poaching a tiger or elephant. As a result, sea cucumbers close to the Andaman Islands have generally thrived. In the ocean around Myanmar , around 50 kilometers (30 miles) further north, it's a different picture. Civil war in the country has severely impacted local livelihoods and local black-market agents are using the instability to offer comparatively higher sums for a boatload of illegally caught sea cucumbers. And as their numbers in local waters dwindle, poachers head south. It is no easy game, however. They have to dodge the Indian coast guard, navy and police, evade local fishermen and even dense populations of crocodiles. Inside the $200 million black market for... sea cucumbers?! To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video They survive on fish, freediving using hookah pipes to breathe, and spend months rationing their diesel to ensure they have enough to make it back home — evading the Myanmar authorities and pirates looking to try and steal their catch. Many poachers are caught by the regional Andaman and Nicobar police, who are being specifically trained to comb the mangrove islands to find them. At least 50 people have been arrested in the past year, some as young as 16 and some in their 60s. Several have come back for the second or third time — risking being incarcerated again after completing full sentences. Is there a way to stop the illegal trade? Despite the efforts of the Indian authorities, the number of poachers coming in, year after year, has stayed stable. Bondaroff sees a need to sound the alarm at a global level. Other similar trades, like that of shark fins, have been slowed thanks to increased awareness about its cruelty and impact on the ecosystem — making it less socially acceptable. Poachers often hide on mangrove islands in the Andamans, making it hard to catch them Image: Dheeraj Aithal/DW "The solution must include educating consumers about the harms of unsustainable and illegal sea cucumber extraction and tackling seafood fraud." Other suggestions include India opening up small areas of its waters where sea cucumbers can be legally fished, or introducing community-based aquaculture that is easier to regulate and would also benefit local fishers. But Bondaroff thinks that tackling the problem also requires cooperation and a deep understanding of the issue. "This means liaising and information sharing between governments and law enforcement agencies," he said. "And working together to address the complex financial crimes that enable sea cucumber crime." This report was supported by the Pulitzer Center. Mint arról a Telexen részletes összefoglalónkban beszámoltunk, egymásnak estek az ukrán és magyar csapat játékosai, miután Nazarenkót kiállították a 92. percben. Szoboszlai Dominikot a játékidő alatt sokszor alattomosan faragták, ami nem egyszer büntetlenül maradt a bíró részéről. Végül Cihankovval szólalkoztak össze, majd Kerkez került közéjük, és vele kezdődött a tülekedés. Ezután mindenki ott termett, és a nézőtérről tárgyat kezdtek bedobálni a futballistákra és a stábtagokra – ezt az M4 videóján meg is lehet nézni . A játékosokat sikerült lecsillapítani, Szoboszlai kapott egy sárga lapot, így folytatódhatott a játék. https://www.digi24.ro/stiri/externe/ue/k.text: Oficialii americani se vor deplasa, joi, la Moscova pentru a-i cere preşedintelui rus Vladimir Putin să-şi dea „binecuvântarea” pentru ca reprezentanţii europeni să poată participa la viitoarele negocieri de pace privind Ucraina, scrie P olitico . Demersul nu este lipsit de provocări pentru Europa. Jared Kushner, ginerele preşedintelui american Donald Trump, care a mediat negocierile la Abu Dhabi, a declarat reporterilor că el şi trimisul Casei Albe, Steve Witkoff, se vor deplasa la Moscova pentru a se întâlni cu liderul rus. Scopul lor este să obţină aprobarea lui Putin pentru ca Europa să aibă un loc la masa negocierilor şi să aprobe ceea ce ar fi cel mai mare schimb de prizonieri de la începutul războiului. Kushner a afirmat că participarea europeană este esenţială pentru discuţiile privind revizuirea viitoarei arhitecturi de securitate a Europei - o cerinţă de lungă durată a Rusiei şi o iniţiativă care a alarmat unii oficiali europeni. „Avem nevoie ca europenii să fie prezenţi la masa negocierilor”, a declarat Kushner pentru P olitico, potrivit News.ro. „I-am transmis direct preşedintelui Putin de mai multe ori, precum şi echipei sale, că singura modalitate de a realiza acest lucru este să-i avem de partea noastră şi cred că sunt deschişi la această idee. Sper că mâine (joi - n.r.), la Moscova, Steve şi cu mine vom avea succes, iar preşedintele Putin îşi va da acordul pentru ca acest lucru să se întâmple. Cred că, dacă va fi de acord cu asta, vom putea face mult mai multe progrese în privinţa problemelor importante”, a spus Kushner. Discuţiile de la Abu Dhabi au fost primele dintre Rusia, Ucraina şi SUA din februarie încoace. Ucraina şi aliaţii săi din Europa au temperat aşteptările privind o evoluţie decisivă în cadrul discuţiilor şi nu s-a anunţat niciun progres cu privire la chestiuni critice precum încetarea focului asupra infrastructurii energetice, transportul maritim pe Marea Neagră sau teritoriul. Însă faptul că părţile s-au întâlnit din nou după nouă luni fără nicio discuţie a fost considerat în capitalele europene un pas important. Într-o mişcare menită să consolideze încrederea între naţiunile aflate în conflict, Kushner a anunţat că Rusia şi Ucraina au convenit asupra a ceea ce va fi probabil „cel mai mare” schimb de prizonieri de la începutul războiului. Cifrele vor fi confirmate joi, a adăugat el. Agenţia de ştiri rusă controlată de stat, Tass, a confirmat că s-a convenit asupra unui schimb de prizonieri „la scară largă”. Kushner a declarat că, în ansamblu, discuţiile de două zile au fost „substanţiale” şi „destul de dure”, dar au reprezentat „un prim pas bun” pentru a readuce cele două părţi la masa negocierilor după o pauză de nouă luni. El a spus că, atunci când oficialii americani s-au întâlnit cu preşedintele ucrainean Volodimir Zelenski la Oslo în urmă cu trei săptămâni, nu era clar dacă Moscova şi Kievul vor putea relua negocierile. „A fost un drum lung pentru a-i readuce pe toţi la masa negocierilor”, a spus Kushner. „Dar cred că aceasta a fost o primă întâlnire foarte bună. A fost o întâlnire dificilă, dar productivă”, a arătat Kushner. El a menţionat că toate problemele relevante au fost discutate între cele două părţi şi că problema teritorială „va fi cea mai greu de rezolvat”. Negociatorii ucraineni au dat vina pe „directivele foarte stricte” venite de la Kremlin pentru limitarea marjei lor de negociere la Abu Dhabi, ceea ce a făcut imposibilă realizarea unor progrese mai mari în cadrul discuţiilor. Kushner şi Witkoff vor încerca să-l convingă pe Putin să deblocheze progresul în anumite chestiuni atunci când se vor întâlni cu acesta joi şi, potrivit oficialilor care au participat la discuţii, să convină asupra datei următoarei runde de negocieri. Ulterior, aceştia se vor deplasa la Dublin pentru a se întâlni cu Zelenski şi, eventual, cu liderii europeni. Ucraina doreşte un acord privind încetarea focului până la Anul Nou, deoarece se teme că Rusia pregăteşte o altă iarnă de bombardamente şi atacuri asupra reţelelor energetice pentru a îngheţa ţara şi a o forţa să se supună. O întrebare crucială, în special pentru Europa, este în ce măsură discuţiile privind schimbarea cadrului de securitate continental susţinut de NATO vor fi legate de negocierile specifice privind pacea în Ucraina. Europenii militează de mult timp pentru ca Ucraina să obţină cele mai solide garanţii de securitate posibile, pentru a împiedica Rusia să atace din nou la sfârşitul acestui război. Oficialii americani doresc să exploreze ideea încheierii cu Ucraina a unui acord de apărare colectivă de tip NATO, care ar putea prevedea chiar ca alianţa însăşi să acţioneze ca garant. Însă Rusia insistă asupra extinderii discuţiilor pentru a include o revizuire a întregii arhitecturi de securitate a Europei - lucru cu care mediatorii americani au fost de acord. Oficialii europeni afirmă că ordinea în care se vor desfăşura aceste discuţii va fi esenţială. Partea europeană şi-a exprimat disponibilitatea de a analiza o reformă a sistemului de securitate mai amplă a continentului pentru a calma îngrijorările Rusiei în paralel cu procesul de pace privind Ucraina. Totuşi, aceştia nu doresc să se angajeze în vreo reformă mai amplă până când nu se va ajunge la pace. Kushner a declarat că scopul este de a discuta toate problemele şi apoi „de a găsi o cale de a le rezolva pe toate în acelaşi timp”. „Cred că este foarte important să avem aceste discuţii”, a spus el. „Dar punerea în aplicare a măsurilor de securitate postbelice nu va avea loc până când nu se va ajunge la un acord privind teritoriul şi toate celelalte chestiuni bilaterale”, a confirmat el. Dorinţa SUA de a implica Europa în negocieri readuce în centrul atenţiei Uniunea Europeană şi alte ţări, precum Regatul Unit, care trebuie să decidă cine le va reprezenta la discuţii. Liderii UE vor analiza această chestiune, devenită acum urgentă, vineri, la Dublin, în cadrul unui summit informal. Zelenski a declarat că doreşte să fie consultat cu privire la cine va reprezenta Europa, dar şi-a îndemnat aliaţii să se grăbească şi, în mod ideal, să aleagă o singură persoană care să preia conducerea în viitoarele discuţii. Kushner a afirmat că actualul aranjament, care include NATO, instituţiile UE şi reprezentanţi din Franţa, Germania, Regatul Unit şi Italia, reprezintă „o modalitate foarte solidă de organizare”, adăugând: „Dacă Europa ar putea identifica o unică persoană care să vorbească în numele său, aceasta ar fi o realizare mai mare decât convingerea ruşilor să o includă în negocieri”.
